parts.gloss: he who is easy of access

words.gloss: he who is easy of access

literal: He who is easy of access, not investigating and not doing justice, that king, by an easy state, himself will perish.
translation: A king who, though easy of access, does not investigate and administer justice, will fall from his position and perish easily of his own accord.
modern: எளிய அணுகுமுறை உடையவனாக இருந்தாலும், வழக்குகளை ஆராய்ந்து நீதி வழங்காத அரசன், வலிமையிழந்து தானாகவே எளிதில் அழிந்துபோவான்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of active justice in governance. While being easy of access (எண்பதத்தான்) is a virtue for a ruler, it becomes meaningless if he fails to investigate grievances (ஓரா) and deliver fair justice (முறைசெய்யா). A king who neglects these core duties will lose his authority and fall to a low, vulnerable state (தண்பதத்தான்), perishing of his own accord (தானே கெடும்) without the need for a powerful external enemy.
